Supply graph (step 5): who buys from whom, with shares and lags

Goods (physical) lag end demand → Nordic, the basis of the forecast kernel: 19 weeks (1.5 quarters; 9–28 weeks across the low / high edge lags). Order signal incl. planning delays (G25): 26 weeks (90% 23–30) flow-weighted, Amazon route 24 weeks (90% 21–27); the forecasts use the goods lag. Hover an edge for its share, lag, inventory holder and evidence; click to pin it. Edges and weights: config/supply_graph.csv, config/supply_graph_weights.csv (Logitech's customer shares per 10-K, point in time).

Reliability. Monte Carlo over every share and lag: goods (physical) mean lag 17–21 weeks (90%). Support is graded separately for the share and for the lag (grade = data support, not the level): Nordic → buyer / own plant: share 100% A/B · lag 0% A/B (100% C); buyer → brand: share 97% A/B (3% C) · lag 0% A/B (100% C); brand → channel: share 94% A/B (6% C) · lag 0% A/B (100% C); distributor → retail: share 0% A/B (100% D) · lag 0% A/B (100% C); retail → end demand: share 100% A/B · lag 100% A/B. 5 D-graded inputs: 5 not public (list: Data gaps). Inputs that move the goods lag most: lag: E08 odm→logitech (grade C, ±1.9 wk), lag: E14 logitech→other_retail (grade C, ±1.5 wk), lag: E01 nordic→nordic_distributors (grade C, ±1.4 wk), lag: E02 nordic→odm (grade C, ±1.1 wk). Planning (information) delays: all grade D; largest input info delay: oem_sop (4 edges) ±3.2 wk (G25).

Logitech's unnamed 56% of sales: how much goes through distributors — evidence and range (G20)

Share of the unnamed 56% sold through smaller distributors: p = 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 (grade D, G20). The 10-K names Amazon, Ingram and TD Synnex; the rest is not split. Edge E14 carries a mixed lag: (1 − p) × direct retail + p × the distributor route. The old setting p = 0 is ruled out by the evidence below.

  • Floor 0.25 (conditional, from C-grade evidence): B2B is about 40% of revenue (R8) while Ingram + TD Synnex are 26% of gross sales (R1). Even if all of the 26% were B2B, at least 14 of the 56 residual points are B2B, and the 10-K says B2B demand reaches Logitech mainly through distributors (R4): p >= 14 / 56 = 0.25. Condition: that residual B2B goes through distributors, not direct to resellers such as CDW or Insight (R6).
  • Cap 0.75 (judgment): the 10-K sells directly to major retail chains with significant shelf space (R5; Best Buy, Walmart, Target, MediaMarkt named in R7), plus Logitech.com and direct resellers, so the residual cannot be nearly all distribution.
  • Mid 0.5 (judgment): rough split of the 56%: direct retail chains ~15-24%, Logitech.com ~2-4%, direct resellers ~3-6%, other distributors (D&H, ALSO / Actebis, Esprinet, Exertis, Copaco, Daiwabo, Digital China: R7) the rest, ~22-36%, i.e. p ~0.4-0.65. EMEA and Asia-Pacific (59% of Logitech's sales over 2025Q3-2026Q2) lean on two-tier distribution; the Americas lean on direct big-box retail.
  • Not found: no filing (SEC full-text search 2001-2026), cached call transcript or reachable conference transcript gives a distributor share of sales. The May 2025 and March 2026 conference transcripts on s1.q4cdn.com return 403.
  • Grade D. The value is not public. The project rule for D would be 0-1; the floor rests on the R8 arithmetic and the cap on R5 / R7, both stated here, so the range is narrower than the rule by design.

The analysis in charts

The forecasts first, then the brief's questions in order: lag, mechanism, attribution, structural breaks, limitations. Every takeaway line is computed from the same data as its chart; SVGs in deliverables/figures/.

Forecasts

How each forecast is built

Each bar is one named term; the last bar is the forecast with its 80% range (whisker) and the company guide (grey band). Nordic Q3 2026: 240 vs guide mid 230; Logitech Q2 FY27: 1,226 vs guide mid 1,202; GN 2,247 DKKm: FY guide + GN's own August-guide habit -> H2 organic +0.15%, then FX.

Source: outputs/forecast_details.json (step 7e guide-error model, 5d incident; 7c chain term = 0)

Lag structure

Reasoned lag vs the data

The graph puts most weight at lag 1 (kernel mean 1.5 quarters, built on the goods lag of 19 weeks); the order signal, which adds the planners' delays, arrives later: 26 weeks over all routes (90% 23–30), 24 on the Amazon route (G25). The data: lag 1 ρ 0.78, lag 2 ρ 0.90, lag 3 ρ 0.84, lag 4 ρ 0.59 (n ≈ 15). A broad plateau, not a sharp peak: the correlation also carries the common industry cycle, so it cannot pick the lag, and the structure sets it.

Source: step 5 graph_kernel.csv, graph_mean_lag_mc.csv (goods lag), graph_signal_lag_mc.csv (order signal, G25); step 4 xcorr_all.csv

Mechanism

The chain over time

Bullwhip in one picture: since mid-2021 Logitech sell-in moved between -22% and 12% YoY, Nordic Consumer between -43% and 63%; Nordic turns after Logitech and overshoots both ways.

Source: outputs/tier_panel.csv; shading: step 3b cycle_state.csv (data-dated channel state)

Where the swing is created

Logitech sell-in vs its own sell-through ×0.99 (close to 1 by construction: the proxy is sell-in + the disclosed gap); purchases ×1.24; Nordic Consumer ×2.7 vs sell-in: the swing is created at the component tier. Ratios by hand-set window are left out: the windows are not the data-dated states (P92) and calm-window ratios are small-denominator artefacts (P04).

Source: steps/step3_inventory_mechanism/outputs/bullwhip_links.csv

Where the inventory sits

Nordic's own inventory (193 days) is not what moves its revenue; distributor and ODM stock is, but ODMs disclose nothing and distributors only all-vendor totals (Arrow / Avnet for chips, Ingram / TD Synnex for finished goods). Logitech's channel: -2.1 wk vs target (-1.1 on the latest anchor; step 3: lean).

Source: step 3 factors_quarterly.csv, channel_index_logitech.csv, channel_call.csv, step3_summary.json; shading: step 3b cycle_state.csv (data-dated channel state)

Attribution

How much of Nordic the chain covers

About 17% of Nordic in 2026Q2 (13–21%; estimate over 2025Q3–2026Q2 16%, 13–20%) runs through Logitech and GN. The chain's direct evidence covers only that slice, but one quarter out Nordic moves ≈3.2× what the slice implies (reasoned chain's back-test slope): its other consumer customers ride the same cycle.

Source: steps/step2_attribution/outputs/attribution_path.csv, attribution.json

Structural breaks

Where the chain link breaks, and where it does not

1 of 7 tested breaks reject stability at 5%: chain link · cycle state lean → building (data-dated) @ 2022Q4. The hand-set regime edges do not (2022Q3 p 0.66, 2024Q2 p 0.77): the break sits at a turn of the data-dated channel state, not at the config regime dates (P92).

Source: step 5c relationship_breaks.csv, event_breaks.csv; shading: step 3b cycle_state.csv (data-dated channel state)

Limitations

Does it work? The back-test

Walk-forward RMSE, information of each forecast date. h=1 (14 quarters): the rule used errs 8.1m (F30 set after seeing these quarters), the GB benchmark 7.4m, the reasoned chain 12.7m (weight 0). h=2 (9 quarters): GRi 25m (chosen after seeing these quarters, F26), GR 28m = plain lag-2 L3 28m, vs 46m for the guide extrapolation: the gain is timing, not the graph (G5, P61).

Source: step 6 walkforward_h2.csv; step 7c chain_nordic_walkforward_h1.csv; step 7e guide_error_walkforward_nordic.csv

Point = guide midpoint × (1 + usual guide error) + supply-chain terms and known events pushed through the supply graph. Usual guide error: Nordic = its own record in the current channel state, with chip-shortage quarters kept apart (a choice made after seeing the data); three alternatives are logged in advance and scored after the print (blended with the peers, the rule before the shortage split, the channel read from Nordic's own words). Logitech = its record blended with 12 peers' plus the channel state; the chain gets no weight. GN = plain average of its own August-guide misses, plus FX at ECB rates since the guide. Margins = guide + own past error where a point guide exists, else the simple rule with the lowest error on past quarters.

Nordic usual guide error +5.23% = own record when the channel was neither building nor short of supply (+5.23%, 15 quarters; building -8.39 pts, 7 quarters; shortage -2.79 pts, 8 quarters; the shortage split was adopted after seeing the data and tests no better than the rule before it), with the channel now 'lean' (+0.00); band: typical error 5.11%; Logitech usual guide error +1.98% = its record +1.98% (own +1.61% on 5 quarters — small sample, own weight 11%, blended with the 12 peers) + channel state 'lean' (+0.00); band: typical error 3.46%.

Channel-state sensitivity (Nordic's own record by channel state; the state is read from distributor inventory days, a supply shortage from live lead times): the channel is 'lean' (2026Q2), so the state adds +0.00 pts. If distributors turn to building, Nordic's own building effect (-8.39 pts; peers -1.64 over 619 peer quarters, t -4.4) takes Nordic from 240.2 to 220.9; building followed 'lean' in 6% of past quarters. If Nordic's supply turns short (live lead time above 26 weeks), its own shortage effect (-2.79 pts, 8 quarters) takes it to 233.8. To watch (Monitor tab): the channel state, Arrow / Avnet inventory days, Nordic's lead times and Nordic's own words.

Change an assumption and re-run the forecasts

Every value in config/model.yaml and every edge lag in config/supply_graph.csv can be edited; Run scenario re-runs the whole model in a sandbox copy of the repository (runs/scenarios/<id>/repo), about 2–3 minutes, and shows the six forecasts beside the committed ones. Run scenario never writes the committed config or outputs; only Save to config writes config/model.yaml / config/supply_graph.csv.

The sandbox needs the local results server: run python scripts/serve.py and open http://127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard, tab Predict. Opened as a file, this page shows the committed run only.

Risks the tests cannot rule out: the composite channel factor (a pre-registered challenger, not in the forecast; B26) and Nordic's own guide-error record (F32)

  • ● R1. Against the 4-quarter benchmark the gain comes from one cycle turn.
    evidence(a) vs the past-4-quarter beat (the gate's benchmark): the three best quarters (2024Q4, 2024Q2, 2024Q3) carry 111% of the gain — above 100% because the other quarters together lose; the composite wins 7 of 11 quarters; over the last six quarters the composite is WORSE (RMSE 1.71 vs 1.67 pts). (b) vs the intercept-only model (mean of all past beats, no factors): the three best quarters (2023Q4, 2024Q4, 2025Q2) carry 106% of the gain — above 100% because the other quarters together lose; the composite wins 7 of 11 quarters (out-of-sample R² +0.46; last six quarters 1.71 vs 3.98). Reading: the composite wins more quarters against the intercept-only model (7 vs 7 of 11) and its top-3 share is lower (106% vs 111%), but against both baselines three quarters still carry most of the gain — the concentration is only partly an artefact of the slow 4-quarter benchmark. Either way the sample holds one cycle.
  • ● R2. Factors chosen after seeing the data.
    evidenceThe four factors were chosen after step 3 had already shown the 2021-2026 data (researcher degrees of freedom). No back-test removes this. The only clean test: Nordic Q3 2026 print, 22 Oct 2026 (pre-registered in steps/step6_backtest/outputs/composite_prereg_log.csv; the last row logged before the print is the forecast of record) — none scored yet.
  • ● R3. The composite and its ridge variant disagree on this quarter.
    evidence2026Q3: composite (equal weights) beat +3.39% vs ridge challenger +1.69% (+1.71 pts = USD 3.9m on the USD 230m midpoint). Which specification is right is unknown until the print.
  • ● R4. Very few independent observations.
    evidenceThe composite has 20 quarterly values but lag-1 autocorrelation 0.75, so it holds about 2.8 independent observations (Bartlett n(1-ρ)/(1+ρ)); the beat itself holds about 8.0 of 19. Every cycle-dependent conclusion rests on roughly one downturn and one upturn; each extra fitted parameter (absolute value, separate +/- slopes, regime switches) would be fitted to those. More independent evidence has to come from more cycles or more companies (peer panel), not from the model's form.
  • ● R5. The channel mechanism itself fails external validation on 12 peers.
    evidencePooled over 442 peer firm-quarters and several cycles, the same channel factors do not beat each firm's own mean beat out of sample (OOS R² -0.009, better in 52% of quarters). On the industry factor Nordic's slope is +2.99 pts per sd vs +0.39 for the peers. A Nordic-like peer set (11 firms, distribution share >= 35%) predicts Nordic's slope from its distribution share at +0.16 (90% PI -0.28 to +0.61); distribution share itself explains nothing (t = 0.2). The composite's Nordic result is most likely specific to one cycle of one company.
  • ● R6. The channel mechanism rests on one cycle turn, for Nordic and for the peers.
    evidencePeers' slope by window: 2008-10 -0.22, 2011-19 +0.19, Nordic's window +0.59 (se 0.92). Three quarters carry 92% of the peers' and 82% of Nordic's slope; 2023Q3, 2023Q4 are in both. Nordic vs peers in the same window: t = 0.9 after autocorrelation.
  • ● R7. The channel state cannot see an end-demand shock.
    evidenceNordic's record runs 2019Q1-2026Q2 (30 guides, F32). Of the 15 quarters that set the habit (channel neither building nor short), 2020Q2, 2020Q3 had the guide raised before the print: errors +10.6, +19.4 against the guide the model scores, +1.7, +3.8 against the last guide, with the state reading 'lean, normal'. The state variable is a channel stock (distributor days); it explains misses when distributors build (2023) and is blind to a demand shock (2020). Habit +5.23% with those quarters, +3.72% without (n 13); before 2021 +6.10% (n 8), from 2021 +4.24% (n 7). The rule is kept as pre-stated (F33); the shock sits in the range, not in a new term.
  • ● R8. The state split has no walk-forward edge on the longer record.
    evidenceWalk-forward over 14 quarters from 2023Q1: rule in force 5.54 pts, guide midpoint (zero error) 5.55, past-4-quarter beat 5.41, pooled with the peers 5.06 (F16 challenger). The habit's sign replicates out of sample (Nordic guided below the outcome in 8 of the 9 quarters 2019Q1-2021Q1), the claim that splitting it by channel state improves the forecast does not; the split is kept for its mechanism (F20, F30), and every challenger is scored at the print.

R1-R4 concern the composite; R5-R6 concern the channel mechanism in general, so they also bound how much weight any channel signal in the forecasts can carry; R7-R8 are what Nordic's own record extended to 2019Q1 shows about the guide-error rule in force (F32; rule kept, F33). ● triggered by the current data · full text: steps/step6_backtest/outputs/step6_report.md, steps/step7_forecast/outputs/guide_error_record_extension.csv

Fiscal calendars: which fiscal quarter is 'Q3 2026' for each company

The three prints cover the same months, Jul-Sep 2026: Nordic Q3, GN Q3 and Logitech Q2 FY2027 (fiscal year ends 31 March). Every other company is lined up the same way: a fiscal period is filed under the calendar quarter that holds most of its days (period end - 45 days, one rule in the code since P124). Bar = the fiscal quarter; blue = the quarters its source table stores agree with that rule, red = some do not, grey = the table stores the quarter only; diamond = report date. For the 6 companies whose source table stores a period end or fiscal label next to the quarter, every stored quarter agrees with the majority rule; the other tables store the calendar quarter only.

The chain over time (step 5b)

Same nodes and links every quarter; inventory, flow and channel state move with the data. The label shows the data-dated channel state (step 3b). Lags are not observed quarter by quarter: only their data bound (inventory cover) moves; the regime multiplier is an assumption. Series and sources: the 'Data & time series' tab.

Node colour = inventory cover vs the node's own 2020-2026 history: lean middle heavy no data. Edge width = share of the Logitech + GN slice (Logitech's 10-K as known that quarter); colour = support for the lag, solid / dashed = support for the share (step 5). Hover an edge: its lag's data bound that quarter (inventory cover, Little's law) and the regime-adjusted lag (assumption: mid lag, E14 p-mixed (G20), times the lag multiplier of the hand-set config regime; P92: the data-dated state differs).

The evidence behind every number, for a reviewer. Each box is rebuilt every run; hand-written labels come from the CSVs named in each box.

Behind the Q4 scenarios: Nordic 2026Q4 graph models (h = 2)

Not one of the three forecast prints. Shown as evidence for the lag structure and the model's limits: the chain adds nothing to a guided quarter (weight 0) but is the best model one quarter past the guide. No company guide exists for this quarter yet. The number is GRi (F26): Logitech's sell-in through the Nordic -> ODM / distributor -> Logitech segment, the unreported quarter filled by our bias-corrected sell-in forecast; walk-forward error 25.4m, 0.54x the guide-based extrapolation (n 9), against GR's 28.0m (0.59x). The gain over GR is a tie within noise and was found after looking (post-hoc, disclosed), and the fill fails F24's bar; it was chosen for the mechanism (Logitech's shipments set its production, which is what its ODMs buy Nordic chips for; the sell-through gap it avoids is unforecastable). Pre-registered (F22, q4_prereg_log.csv): GR (sell-through proxy, persistence fill) and the chain as reasoned (CH) are the challengers. The graph models still regress all Nordic consumer revenue on Logitech: a proxy for the common consumer cycle, not only the Logitech / GN slice; they fail when Logitech diverges from the rest of consumer electronics (e.g. the 2026 supplier incident).

Key insights (computed from the data)
  1. The beat is management's forecast error, not demand. A factor can predict the beat only if management ignored public information; channel signals can at most help the revenue forecast beyond the guided quarter (K4).
    evidenceAcross 632 peer quarters revenue YoY has sd 29% but the beat only 3.9% (correlation 0.23). In the 20 quarters where a peer's revenue fell 30% or more YoY the mean beat was -0.2% and 95% stayed within +/-5%: management writes the cycle into the guide.
  2. Nordic's 2023Q3 miss was not set up by a guide more optimistic than the peers'. Which comparator is 'the market' decides the reading; the pre-registered peer median does not flag the episode.
    evidenceFor 2023Q3 Nordic guided +0.5% q/q against a peer median of +0.4% (relative optimism +0.1 pts), then missed by 12.9%: the shortfall arose inside the quarter. Against the consumer-heavy peers only (exploratory, chosen after seeing the data) the gap was +18.8 pts.
  3. No guide-setting factor predicts misses. The large Nordic misses are rare intra-quarter surprises; about a dozen candidate factors have now been tried on 21 quarters, so any one that 'works' on Nordic alone is expected by chance.
    evidenceRelative guidance optimism on 671 peer firm-quarters (70 quarters): +0.005 per pt (t 0.3); walk-forward OOS R2 -0.005 vs each firm's mean; the most optimistic fifth of guides misses in 15% of quarters, the least optimistic in 24%. On Nordic without 2023Q3, 2023Q4: last_beat keep |t| >= 2; the channel factor keeps +0.86 (t 0.7, naive).
  4. Beyond the guided quarter the channel factor adds little to revenue forecasts. Where the channel belongs (revenue beyond the guide, not the beat) is consistent with (not confirmed by) the data: its value there is small and turn-dependent: seasonality does more than the channel.
    evidenceForecasting revenue one quarter past the guide (g2 = actual t+1 / guide t) on 479 peer firm-quarters: seasonal benchmark + channel factor gives OOS R2 +1.6% vs the seasonal benchmark alone (t 1.4; RMSE 10.55 with the channel vs 10.64 seasonal vs 11.54 flat, pts); 102% of the gain comes from 2023Q3, 2023Q4, 2025Q4; without 2023Q3, 2023Q4 +0.3%.

Mechanism: who holds the inventory, and who discloses it

Own balance-sheet inventory is disclosed as a number by every listed company; channel inventory, the part that moves the next tier's orders, is disclosed as a number by one company in the chain's reach (Microchip's distributor days) and only in words by Logitech, GN and Nordic. Every model series that stands in for a hidden quantity is named in the last column (grades in the Data tab). Source: steps/step3_inventory_mechanism/config/inventory_disclosure.csv.

Guidance track record: how accurate, how conservative

Each forecast anchors on the company's guide, so this is the evidence behind each uplift and range. Error = actual minus guide midpoint (% of the midpoint for USD guides, points for growth and margins). Label rule fixed before the numbers: conservative = mean error > 0 and ≥ 70% of outcomes at or above the midpoint; aggressive = the mirror; mixed otherwise; fewer than 4 outcomes = too few. Sources: company releases, every number quote-checked (Pipeline A: logitech_guidance_history.csv, gn_guidance_history.csv, nordic_quarterly.csv).

  • Nordic — quarterly revenue range (all): conservative (median +2.5 %, mean +2.5, sd 5.9, n=30, in range 70%); quarterly gross-margin floor: conservative (median +1.3 pts, mean +1.2, sd 2.7, n=30, in range 70%); quarterly revenue range (normal): conservative (median +4.0 %, mean +4.2, sd 3.0, n=11, in range 82%)
  • Logitech — annual op_income_usdm: initial guide (>= 6 months ahead): conservative (median +10.1 %, mean +44.8, sd 93.1, n=6, in range 0%); annual sales: initial guide (>= 6 months ahead): conservative (median +4.3 %, mean +11.9, sd 27.8, n=6, in range 33%); quarterly sales range (from Q1 FY26): conservative (median +1.9 %, mean +1.6, sd 0.6, n=5, in range 60%)
  • GN — annual ebita_margin_pct, audio/group: initial guide (>= 6 months ahead): aggressive (median -1.6 pts, mean -2.0, sd 2.3, n=5, in range 40%); annual organic_growth_pct, audio/group: initial guide (>= 6 months ahead): aggressive (median -4.0 pts, mean -4.2, sd 5.3, n=5, in range 20%)

The guide error each forecast applies (Logitech F16; Nordic F20/F30; GN F17/F23)

  • Nordic: own record by the data-dated channel state of t−1 (F20, F30): its mean miss when the channel was neither building nor in a supply shortage, +5.23% on 15 of its 30 guides, plus its own building effect (-8.39 pts, 7 quarters) or shortage effect (-2.79 pts, 8 quarters) when t−1 was in that state.
  • Logitech: habit pooled with 12 peers' quarterly guides (F16; peers' mean +2.02%, spread 0.55; weight 11% on its own 5 guides), plus the peers' building effect -1.64 pts (t -4.4, 619 peer firm-quarters) when t−1 was building.
  • GN: plain mean of its own August full-year organic-guide misses (F17, F23), -3.3 pts on 5 years; no state term (the peers' effect is a quarterly % revenue miss).

Units: % of the guide midpoint (GN: pts of full-year organic growth). sd = predictive sd; the 80% range is ±1.28 sd.

Lag: Amazon sell-out → Nordic revenue, edge by edge

≈24 weeks (1.9 quarters) order-signal lag (physical dwell alone 17 wk + the buyers' planning delay, G25) = edge 1 4 wk (Amazon cuts orders to Logitech) + edge 2 20 wk (Logitech's build and chip orders reach Nordic); 90% 21–27 wk (graph Monte Carlo, step 5); 12–37 if each edge sits anywhere in its prior independently. Set by the chain's structure; the edge-by-edge regressions could not narrow it.

    Amazon / Ingram Micro / TD Synnex --edge 1--> Logitech / GN --edge 2--> Nordic
    edge 1 = customers' sell-out -> their orders to the brand (= brand sell-in)
    edge 2 = brand sell-in -> build / component orders -> Nordic revenue (ODM / EMS and Nordic's distributors folded in)

What it says

  • Edge 1 is short by structure; the quarterly data cannot confirm it. The prior 7.0 (2.1–12.4) wk comes from the customers' inventory cover (evidence above). The channel index's reversion gives a median-unbiased mean lag of 27.6 (0.0–∞) wk (rho 0.62, 90% -0.01–1.00, n 13); the interval runs from full correction within the quarter to no reversion, so the posterior is the prior. The plain OLS reading, 10 wk (bootstrap 0–20), would look like a confirmation only because OLS rho on ~13 quarters is biased towards zero (P90). A lag under one quarter is below what quarterly data resolve, except through this reversion speed.
  • Edge 2 is sized by attribution and timed by structure. With Logitech's slice fixed at s × m = 0.25 (share of Nordic consumer 25% × slice multiplier 1.00), every lag from 0 to 52 wk is inside the 90% profile set; across the 9 constrained fits the 90% interval covers 100% of 0–52 wk. The data fail to contradict the prior and cannot confirm it: posterior 19.6 (7.0–31.3) wk (= the prior). Left free, the slope is 1.40, 5.5× the slice: what a free fit times is the common cycle, not Logitech's orders (P77, P91).
  • Amazon sell-out → Nordic revenue ≈ 24 weeks (1.9 quarters): edge 1 4.5 + edge 2 19.6 wk; 90% range 12–37 wk with the edges independent, 8–39 if they stretch together. Through Ingram / TD Synnex 29 wk; flow-weighted over Logitech's routes 27 wk (GN 26 wk). These are order-signal lags; the physical dwell alone is 17 / 20 / 19 wk: the rest is the buyers' planning (review period + forecast smoothing, grade D, G25).
  • Regime dependence. The fits use the destock and normal quarters only: in 2020Q3–2022Q2 Nordic revenue was wafer supply, and config stretches the lag ×2 there. Normal quarters alone (n 9) cover 100% of the range; a destock intercept gives tau 39 wk with 100% covered - no regime pins edge 2. Edge 1's persistence (median-unbiased 28 wk) comes from a sample that starts in the destock (channel +4.1 wk vs target in 2023Q1, +1.7 wk by 2024Q2): if real, it is a drain of the channel target, not the reorder lag of a normal channel, so the normal-channel prior stands.

Structural breaks through the chain: shocks vs breaks (step 5d)

A shock leaves every edge as it is and the graph carries it; a break changes an edge (lag, share, amplitude) or the reporting basis. Worked example: Logitech's 2026 supplier incident pushed back node by node (per-row scale).

Live gauge: Nordic's Bluetooth LE SoCs at authorized distributors (2026-09-26)

nRF is Nordic's part-number prefix: the nRF52, nRF53 and nRF54 families are its Bluetooth Low Energy SoCs, the chips inside wireless mice, keyboards and headsets; the brief names nRF52 and nRF54 parts as the gauge of Nordic's channel tightness.

PartAuthorized stock (units)Distributor groupsChange vs 2026-09-23 (like for like)Factory lead time1k price (median)
nRF52832-QFAA-R1,8494+0% on 4 of 9 listings seen beforenot quoted$2.48
nRF52833-QIAA-R03no listing in commonnot quoted$3.28
nRF52840-QIAA-R16,6964+0% on 4 of 9 listings seen beforenot quoted$4.03
nRF5340-QKAA-R3,0003+0% on 3 of 8 listings seen before16 wk (read 2026-09-22)$6.04
nRF54L15-QFAA-R2,1332+0% on 2 of 7 listings seen before16 wk (read 2026-09-22)$2.05

Readings on demand (./run.sh --live takes a new one), not a series: listings vary by region and fetch (e.g. Avnet Silica on one day, Avnet Americas on another), so the change compares only the exact listings present in both readings, and there is no public history to back-test. One reading enters the model: a latest lead time above 26 weeks turns Nordic's state to shortage (D24, config cycle_state.shortage.lead_time_min_weeks); stock and price enter nothing. Lead time also bounds the Nordic direct-order lag (step 5); stock reads channel tightness; the 1k price reads pricing. Source: findchips (Digi-Key / Mouser block scripts; Mouser API used when MOUSER_API_KEY is set).

Lag and mechanism — charts and the reasoned lag

Reasoned end-to-end lag sell-out → Nordic revenue: 15/22/32 weeks (≈1.69 quarters) in a normal channel (single-chain reasoning); Drawn as a graph (step 5: Amazon direct 18%, Ingram / TD Synnex 26% of Logitech's gross sales, 10KFY26): goods (physical) dwell 19 weeks (90% 17–21); order signal incl. planning delays 26 weeks (90% 23–30) flow-weighted, Amazon route 24 weeks (90% 21–27) (G25). In the 2020Q3–2022Q2 supply-constrained regime (Nordic's backlog peaked at 9.9x quarterly revenue in 2021Q4), config stretches edge 2 x2: 37 weeks (≈2.8 quarters) at the mid. Documented, not applied: those quarters are excluded from the fits (D13). Observed: Nordic Consumer turned negative YoY 4 quarters after Logitech (2021Q4 → 2022Q4), one turning point. Correlation with Logitech sell-in peaks at lag 2 quarter(s): the industry cycle's timing at Nordic, not the chain lag (semiconductor billings and US electronics sales give the same timing; one cycle cannot pin the lag - step 4 L2, P86); amplitude ratio Nordic/Logitech = 2.6x in the destock, 5.1x in the recovery. Logitech + GN ≈ 16% of Nordic revenue (p10–p90 13–20%; ≤ 11% if invoiced direct — route unknown; grade B); PC-peripherals category ≈ 18% of total.

Back-test: lag models vs guidance

Lag-model error relative to guidance + real-time beat on the same quarters — next quarter (guided): 3.93–5.90×; the quarter after: 0.54–0.61× (below 1 = better than the carried guide). Nordic guides from its own order book, so a lagged Logitech signal adds nothing for the guided quarter. Full report: steps/step6_backtest/outputs/step6_report.md.

P86step 5 vs step 4 lag
physical dwell-time lag vs order-signal lag; like-with-like drivers; common cycle; flat correlation surface (one cycle); interpolation smoothing bias		Step 4's measured 2-quarter (26-week) peak looked 7 weeks longer than the graph's 19. But the driver is Logitech revenue (sell-in), whose like-with-like lag is the graph's upstream 14.3 weeks: on a continuous lag the peak is 31 weeks (90% CI 19-36), which excludes 14.3 and step 4's own upstream 15. Nordic lags US electronics-store sales (18-20 weeks) and WSTS semiconductor billings (26 weeks) by amounts that cannot be told from its lag behind Logitech (paired-difference CIs include 0). The graph's edge lags are Little's-law dwell times at 2026Q2 cover (Logitech 66 days vs 120 in 2022Q2); order signals add forecast smoothing, planning cycles, batching and lead time without holding stock. A lag search whose sample changes with the lag also moves the peak

The correlation surface is flat: Logitech's series starts 2022Q2, so there is one down-up cycle and 13-18 quarters; on the fixed 13-quarter sample every tau from ~1.5 to ~2.75 quarters (19-36 weeks) is within 0.03 of the maximum correlation (near-optimal set, graph_vs_step4_continuous_lag.csv). shock direction / causality		One lead-shift formula applied to every shock: a demand shock (end demand changes) propagates forward through the order-signal lag, Nordic(t) = sum_k kernel_k D(t-k); a dated supply or event shock propagates forward from its date (shipments before it are sunk; what a backward shift would place before the date becomes stock at the holder, used at restart, total conserved).
